note: A rectified street-panorama crop of one Amsterdam house front; the house in question fills the image.

hoist.instructions: Does the house front in `facade` have a hoist beam (a projecting timber beam with a hook or pulley under the gable top, for lifting goods)?

criteria.true: A hoist beam or hook projects from the gable top.

stoop.instructions: Is there a stoop (outside steps leading UP from the pavement to the front door, which is a floor above the pavement) on the house front in `facade`?

criteria.true: Steps rise from the pavement to a raised front door.
criteria.false: The front door is at pavement level.

souterrain.instructions: Is there a souterrain entrance (a door or window BELOW pavement level, reached by steps going down, under the stoop or beside the front)?

criteria.true: A below-street-level door or basement window with steps or a well in front.

erker.instructions: Does the house front in `facade` have a bay window (erker: a window box that projects forward from the wall, usually on one or more upper storeys)?

balcony.instructions: Does the house front in `facade` have a balcony or a balustrade/railing in front of a French window?

criteria.true: A balcony or railing is in front of a window or door opening.

door_present.instructions: Is the main front door of the house visible in `facade`?

criteria.true: A front door of this house is visible.
criteria.false: No front door visible (out of frame, hidden, or all shop windows).

door.instructions: The main front door of the house in `facade`.

shopfront.instructions: Does the ground floor of the house front in `facade` have a shopfront (large display windows, a shop or cafe front, a fascia or a sign)?

criteria.true: The ground floor is a shop, cafe or other commercial front.

shop_box.instructions: The shopfront (ground floor commercial front) of the house in `facade`.
